manifesto.paragraphOne: Herocasa was born on Lake Garda from the direct experience of people who own a second home and know how complex it is to turn it into revenue without giving up their time.
manifesto.paragraphTwo: We are not a portal, not an OTA. We are a local team that answers the phone, meets your guests, knows the trusted plumber in every town on the lake — and leaves the house exactly as you handed it over.

services.intro: Six work streams, one point of contact. Managing your home is one service, not a series of quotes.

list.title: Full bureaucracy management
list.body: CIN registration, SUAP filings, police notifications, ISTAT, tourist tax, flat-rate tax. All compliant, so you never have to think about it again.

list.title: Multi-channel dynamic pricing
list.body: Airbnb, Booking, VRBO, direct channel. Prices revised every day based on seasonality, events, and local demand — to maximize net yield.

list.title: Personal 24/7 check-in
list.body: Guests are welcomed and looked after step by step, from arrival to departure, at any hour.

list.title: Professional cleaning & linen
list.body: In-house trained cleaning team, rented linen sheets, quality check after every check-out. The house is always ready.

list.title: Maintenance & small repairs
list.body: Network of trusted craftsmen in every town on the lake. Coordination, transparent quotes, approval above threshold.

list.title: Transparent monthly reports
list.body: Owner dashboard with occupancy, gross revenue, costs, net. Downloadable statement every month. Honest reporting on your asset.

process.intro: From first contact to first guest in a few weeks. Every phase agreed with you, every cost declared up front.

steps.title: Call & site visit
steps.body: You tell us about the house, your goals, personal-use constraints. We book a free site visit, no commitment.

steps.title: Analysis & yield plan
steps.body: We give you a realistic projection of occupancy, prices, expected net income. With historical data and local comparables.

steps.title: Onboarding & listing
steps.body: Transparent contract, professional photos, staging, channel opening. Nothing to do on your side.

steps.title: Management & reporting
steps.body: From here on, silence. Every month a report and a bank transfer. You come back to your house whenever you want.

list.q: How much will I earn with Herocasa?
list.a: It depends on town, type, seasonality and state of the property. On average, owners moving from self-managed listings see net yield grow 20-35% in the first year. The free valuation will give you a reasoned estimate based on your real coordinates.

We charge a percentage of gross revenue, with no setup cost, no monthly subscription, no hidden fees. The exact percentage depends on the service tier (base or full concierge) and we tell you in the quote, before signing.

We do. Fully. CIN registration, SUAP filings, daily police notifications, ISTAT, payment of tourist tax to the town. You receive a summary. If you already have a VAT number, we coordinate with your accountant.

list.q: Can I use my home whenever I want?
list.a: Always. It is your house. Just flag the personal-use dates in our calendar (email or dashboard) and we block them. We recommend a few weeks' notice to avoid cancelling confirmed bookings, but it is not required.

list.q: What if a guest damages something?
list.a: We inspect the property after every check-out. Small damage is refunded from the deposit. Bigger damage triggers Airbnb AirCover or our supplementary insurance for direct bookings. Either way, you get the house back in the state you handed it to us, or the equivalent refund.

list.q: Which portals do you publish on?
list.a: Airbnb, Booking.com, VRBO, Expedia, and direct on the Herocasa site. The calendar is synced in real time to avoid double bookings. Multi-channel distribution is what maximises occupancy without dropping prices.

list.q: Who pays utilities and routine maintenance?
list.a: Utilities remain in the owner's name and are settled in the monthly report based on actual consumption. Routine maintenance (small work under an agreed threshold) is advanced by us and itemised in the report. Anything above threshold is always approved in advance.

list.q: How does the monthly report work?
list.a: Every month, by the 10th, you receive a PDF report by email with: last month's bookings, occupancy rates, gross revenue per channel, costs (cleaning, linen, portal commissions, tourist tax), net transferred to your account. The transfer arrives at the same time. Total transparency.

peschiera-del-garda.intro1: Peschiera del Garda is the lake's gateway: the station on the Milan–Venice line, the motorway exit and the theme parks a few minutes away bring guests for much of the year, not just in high season.

highlights.title: Easy arrivals all year
highlights.body: Station, motorway and Verona airport close by: guests arrive easily, even for short stays.

highlights.title: A UNESCO historic centre
highlights.body: The Venetian fortress and the old town between the canals draw visitors out of season too.

highlights.title: Families and theme parks
highlights.body: Gardaland and the other parks nearby bring families looking for apartments and homes with several bedrooms.

lazise.intro1: Lazise combines a walled medieval village and its lakefront with a strategic spot on the Verona shore, minutes from the theme parks: a mix that fills the calendar with both couples and families.

highlights.title: Village and lakefront
highlights.body: The walls, the Scaliger castle and the lakeside promenade make Lazise one of the most sought-after places on the Verona shore.

highlights.title: Demand from families
highlights.body: Being close to Gardaland and the water parks brings family bookings, often for several nights.

highlights.title: A long season
highlights.body: Markets, events and the lively lakefront keep bookings coming from spring to autumn.

castelnuovo-del-garda.intro1: Castelnuovo del Garda is home to Gardaland, a stone's throw from the lake and the motorway: houses and villas with gardens inland are much in demand among families and groups looking for space and quiet minutes from the beaches.

highlights.title: Home of Gardaland
highlights.body: Italy's best-known theme park brings guests all season long, weekends outside summer included.

highlights.title: Space and gardens
highlights.body: Detached houses and villas with gardens suit families and groups, who stay longer.

highlights.title: Close to the whole lake
highlights.body: Peschiera, Lazise and Sirmione are a few minutes' drive away.

bardolino.intro1: Bardolino is the lake of wine: the lakefront, the cycle path and the Bardolino DOC wineries attract couples and wine lovers, with a season that stretches into the autumn harvest.

highlights.title: Wine tourism
highlights.body: Wineries and wine events such as the Festa dell'Uva bring guests in September and October too.

highlights.title: Lakefront and cycle path
highlights.body: The promenade and the cycle path towards Garda and Lazise are among the most loved on the lake.

highlights.title: Guests who come back
highlights.body: Couples and friends who choose Bardolino tend to return: reviews and a well-kept home make the difference.

sirmione.intro1: Sirmione is one of the best-known places on Lake Garda: the Scaliger castle, the Grottoes of Catullus and the spa draw international guests all year round, with average prices among the highest on the lake.

highlights.title: Tourism all year
highlights.body: The spa and the old town keep demand alive outside summer, not just in peak months.

highlights.title: International guests
highlights.body: Most guests come from abroad: well-written listings in several languages and quick replies are decisive.

highlights.title: High prices, high expectations
highlights.body: In Sirmione guests pay more and expect more: cleaning, welcome and details keep the rating high.

desenzano-del-garda.intro1: Desenzano is the largest town on the southern lake: station, harbour, restaurants and nightlife keep it lively all year, with demand that mixes holidays, weekends and business stays.

highlights.title: Well connected
highlights.body: Station, motorway and the Verona and Brescia airports nearby: easy to reach even for a weekend.

highlights.title: A town alive all year
highlights.body: Restaurants, shops and events keep demand going in low season too.

highlights.title: Not just holidays
highlights.body: Besides tourists, Desenzano attracts business travellers: frequent short stays and a fuller calendar.

padenghe-sul-garda.intro1: Padenghe sul Garda, in the heart of the Valtènesi, is for those who want peace and quiet: the castle, the hills of olive groves and vineyards and the villas with pools attract guests looking to relax away from the crowds.

highlights.title: Relaxation and nature
highlights.body: The hills, olive groves and vineyards of the Valtènesi: guests look for peace and open space, and are willing to pay for it.

highlights.title: Villas with pools
highlights.body: Homes with a pool and garden are the most requested and allow longer stays.

highlights.title: Close to everything
highlights.body: Desenzano, Salò and the beaches of the southern lake are a few minutes' drive away.

garda.intro1: Garda gives the lake its name and is one of the best-loved villages on the Verona shore: the lakefront on its bay, Punta San Vigilio and nearby Bardolino draw guests, many from Germany, all season long.

highlights.title: The village that named the lake
highlights.body: Lakefront, old town and a sheltered bay: a name guests are already searching for before they leave home.

highlights.title: International guests
highlights.body: A large share of guests come from Germany and Austria: listings in several languages and quick replies make the difference.

highlights.title: Between Bardolino and Punta San Vigilio
highlights.body: Cycle path, beaches and restaurants nearby: ideal for week-long stays.

torri-del-benaco.intro1: Torri del Benaco, with its Scaliger castle on the harbour and the ferry to the Brescia shore, is for guests who want an authentic, quiet village with Monte Baldo behind it.

highlights.title: An authentic village
highlights.body: Harbour, castle and narrow lanes: guests look for atmosphere and quiet, and book longer stays.

highlights.title: Linked to both shores
highlights.body: The ferry to Maderno and the lakeside road make Garda, Malcesine and the Brescia shore easy to reach.

highlights.title: Lake views
highlights.body: Homes with a terrace or lake view are among the most requested and command higher prices.

malcesine.intro1: Malcesine pairs a Scaliger castle on the water with the Monte Baldo cable car: sailing, windsurfing, cycling and hiking bring active guests from spring to autumn, many from Germany, Austria and the Netherlands.

highlights.title: Sport and nature
highlights.body: Reliable wind for sailing and windsurfing, trails and slopes on Monte Baldo: demand that goes beyond summer.

highlights.title: A long season
highlights.body: Spring and autumn are strong months thanks to sporty guests: more nights sold over the year.

highlights.title: Guests from northern Europe
highlights.body: German and Dutch guests are loyal and book well in advance.

salo.intro1: Salò has one of the most elegant lakefronts on Lake Garda and a town centre that is lively all year: shops, restaurants, events and the nearby Vittoriale attract guests looking for quality and comfort.

highlights.title: A lively town all year
highlights.body: Shops, restaurants and events keep demand going outside the season too.

highlights.title: Discerning guests
highlights.body: Guests who choose Salò expect well-kept homes and reliable service, and pay accordingly.

highlights.title: Base for the Brescia riviera
highlights.body: Gardone, the Vittoriale and the Valtènesi are minutes away.

manerba-del-garda.intro1: Manerba del Garda, with its Rocca and the beaches of the Valtènesi, is a classic choice for families and nature lovers: villas with gardens and homes near the lake are booked for one- or two-week stays.

highlights.title: Rocca and beaches
highlights.body: The Rocca di Manerba park and the beaches of the southern lake are the main draw.

highlights.title: Families and longer stays
highlights.body: Families book homes with gardens and several bedrooms, often for a week or more.

highlights.title: Heart of the Valtènesi
highlights.body: Wineries, olive groves and nearby villages stretch the season into autumn.

moniga-del-garda.intro1: Moniga del Garda is a small village with a castle and harbour in the heart of the Valtènesi, home of Chiaretto wine: quiet beaches and vineyard landscapes attract couples and families looking to relax.

highlights.title: A quiet village
highlights.body: Castle, harbour and small beaches: a relaxed alternative to the busier towns.

highlights.title: Land of Chiaretto
highlights.body: Vineyards and wineries of the Valtènesi bring wine-loving guests, even late in the season.

highlights.title: Villas and homes with gardens
highlights.body: Homes with outdoor space are the most requested and allow higher prices.

soiano-del-lago.intro1: Soiano del Lago overlooks the bay from above: a hill village with a castle, olive groves and villas with pools, perfect for guests who want lake views and peace a few minutes from the beaches.

highlights.title: Views over the bay
highlights.body: The hills above the lake offer views that make a difference in photos and reviews.

highlights.title: Villas with pools
highlights.body: A pool and garden are the most sought-after features and allow longer stays.

highlights.title: Close to everything
highlights.body: Padenghe, Manerba and Desenzano are a few minutes' drive away.

lonato-del-garda.intro1: Lonato del Garda combines its Rocca and old town with the Lido on the lake, a stone's throw from Desenzano and the motorway: spacious homes at more accessible purchase prices, with solid tourist demand.

highlights.title: Rocca and Lido
highlights.body: The historic village and lake access bring two kinds of guests to the same area.

highlights.title: Easy to reach
highlights.body: Motorway, Desenzano station and airports nearby: easy arrivals even for a weekend.

highlights.title: Room for families and groups
highlights.body: Houses and villas with gardens host families and groups who stay longer.

valeggio-sul-mincio.intro1: Valeggio sul Mincio, with Borghetto and the Sigurtà Garden Park, is one of the most photographed places inland from Lake Garda: minutes from Peschiera and the theme parks, it attracts couples, families and cyclists.

highlights.title: Borghetto and Sigurtà
highlights.body: The village on the Mincio and the garden park bring visitors from spring to autumn.

highlights.title: The Mincio cycle path
highlights.body: The Peschiera–Mantua cycle path brings cyclists looking for stays of a few nights.

highlights.title: Close to the lake and the parks
highlights.body: Peschiera, Gardaland and the southern lake are fifteen minutes away.

pozzolengo.intro1: Pozzolengo, on the morainic hills between Desenzano and Peschiera, is Lugana and golf country: farmhouses, villas and agriturismi attract guests looking for space and quiet a few minutes from Sirmione.

highlights.title: The Lugana hills
highlights.body: Lugana vineyards and wineries draw wine-loving guests.

highlights.title: Space and quiet
highlights.body: Farmhouses and villas with gardens suit families and groups who stay longer.

highlights.title: Minutes from the lake
highlights.body: Sirmione, Desenzano and Peschiera are very close.

brenzone-sul-garda.intro1: Brenzone sul Garda is a string of small lakeside villages between Torri and Malcesine, with Monte Baldo behind: quiet beaches, small harbours and trails attract guests, many from northern Europe, looking for calm and nature.

highlights.title: Villages on the water
highlights.body: Small harbours and secluded beaches: the authentic feel many guests look for and mention in reviews.

highlights.title: Nature and trails
highlights.body: Monte Baldo is right there: hikers and cyclists stretch the season.

highlights.title: Loyal guests
highlights.body: German and Austrian guests come back year after year and book early.

costermano-sul-garda.intro1: Costermano sul Garda sits on the hills above Garda: villas and homes with lake views, olive groves and golf courses attract guests who want space and quiet a few minutes from the beaches.

highlights.title: Lake views from the hills
highlights.body: Wide views over the Bay of Garda: value you see at once in photos and prices.

highlights.title: Golf and relaxation
highlights.body: The golf courses nearby bring discerning guests in spring and autumn too.

highlights.title: Close to the lake
highlights.body: Garda, Bardolino and the beaches are a few minutes' drive away.

cavaion-veronese.intro1: Cavaion Veronese is Bardolino's hinterland of vineyards and hills: homes with gardens at more accessible purchase prices, a few minutes from the lake, with tourist demand growing every year.

highlights.title: Bardolino wine country
highlights.body: Vineyards and wineries bring wine-loving guests.

highlights.title: Space at a good price
highlights.body: Homes and villas with gardens earn well on a smaller investment.

highlights.title: Close to the lake
highlights.body: Bardolino, Garda and Lazise are minutes away.

affi.intro1: Affi is the gateway to the lake for anyone arriving from the Brenner: the motorway exit, services and closeness to Bardolino and Garda make it a convenient base for families and groups.

highlights.title: Easy to reach
highlights.body: The Affi exit on the Brenner motorway brings guests from Germany and Austria in minutes.

highlights.title: Base for the whole lake
highlights.body: Bardolino, Garda, Lazise and Monte Baldo are close by.

highlights.title: Spacious homes
highlights.body: Villas and houses with gardens host families and groups who stay longer.

caprino-veronese.intro1: Caprino Veronese lies at the foot of Monte Baldo, among woods, pastures and villages: agriturismi, farmhouses and homes with views attract guests looking for nature, sport and fresh air near the lake.

highlights.title: Nature and mountains
highlights.body: Trails, mountain biking and paragliding on Monte Baldo bring active guests for much of the year.

highlights.title: Farmhouses and agriturismi
highlights.body: Country houses and restored farmhouses are much in demand among families and groups.

highlights.title: The lake close by
highlights.body: Garda and Torri del Benaco are a few minutes' drive away.

san-zeno-di-montagna.intro1: San Zeno di Montagna is a plateau high above the lake, over Torri and Garda: spectacular views, cool summer air and chestnut woods attract guests looking for scenery and quiet.

highlights.title: The balcony over the lake
highlights.body: Some of the finest views on Lake Garda: homes with a view are the most photographed and booked.

highlights.title: Cool in summer
highlights.body: While the lake is hot, the plateau stays cool: a strong selling point in peak months.

highlights.title: Nature all year
highlights.body: Hiking, cycling and the chestnut season stretch the calendar into autumn.

pastrengo.intro1: Pastrengo, on the morainic hills between Lazise and the Adige valley, combines quiet and location: villas and homes with gardens a few minutes from the lake, Gardaland and the area's parks.

highlights.title: Hills and quiet
highlights.body: A relaxed alternative to the lakeside towns, with more space and less traffic.

highlights.title: Close to the parks
highlights.body: Gardaland and the other parks nearby bring families all season.

highlights.title: Villas with gardens
highlights.body: Homes with outdoor space are the most requested for multi-night stays.

sommacampagna.intro1: Sommacampagna, between Verona and the lake, is Custoza wine country and minutes from the airport: a location that brings tourists, Verona visitors and business travellers, with demand all year.

highlights.title: Between Verona and the lake
highlights.body: Guests combine the city, the Arena and the lake in one stay.

highlights.title: Not just holidays
highlights.body: Verona's trade fairs and companies bring business stays outside the season too.

highlights.title: Near the airport
highlights.body: Verona airport and the motorway are minutes away: easy arrivals even for a weekend.

san-felice-del-benaco.intro1: San Felice del Benaco, facing the Isola del Garda, is one of the most elegant places in the Valtènesi: beaches, small harbours and fine villas attract high-end guests.

highlights.title: The Isola del Garda
highlights.body: Views of the island and the beaches are a strong draw in photos and listings.

highlights.title: Fine villas
highlights.body: Villas with pool and garden command some of the highest prices on the Brescia shore.

highlights.title: Heart of the Valtènesi
highlights.body: Wineries, olive groves and nearby villages stretch the season.

puegnago-del-garda.intro1: Puegnago del Garda overlooks the Valtènesi from its hills: vineyards, olive groves and homes with pools and lake views attract couples and families looking for relaxation and good wine.

highlights.title: Lake views among the vines
highlights.body: Views over the hills and lake that make a difference in reviews.

highlights.title: Homes with pools
highlights.body: A pool and garden are the most sought-after features and allow longer stays.

highlights.title: Wine tourism
highlights.body: Valtènesi wineries bring guests late in the season too.

polpenazze-del-garda.intro1: Polpenazze del Garda is a Valtènesi hill village with a castle and vineyards: quiet, minutes from the beaches, ideal for guests looking for countryside and peace near the lake.

highlights.title: Village and castle
highlights.body: The historic hilltop centre is an authentic alternative to the lakeside towns.

highlights.title: Wine country
highlights.body: Chiaretto vineyards and wineries attract wine lovers and couples.

highlights.title: Space and quiet
highlights.body: Farmhouses and villas with gardens suit families and groups.

gardone-riviera.intro1: Gardone Riviera is the most refined stretch of the lake: the Vittoriale, the botanical garden and historic villas attract high-end guests interested in culture, elegance and impeccable service.

highlights.title: The Vittoriale
highlights.body: D'Annunzio's estate draws visitors all year, out of season too.

highlights.title: High-end guests
highlights.body: Guests who choose Gardone expect well-kept homes and matching hospitality, and pay accordingly.

highlights.title: Mild climate
highlights.body: The sheltered riviera favours stays in spring and autumn as well.

toscolano-maderno.intro1: Toscolano-Maderno combines a lakefront, wide beaches and the Valley of the Paper Mills: with the ferry to Torri del Benaco it is a convenient base for families who want to explore both shores.

highlights.title: Beaches and lakefront
highlights.body: Wide beaches and lakeside walks are perfect for families with children.

highlights.title: Linked to both shores
highlights.body: The ferry to Torri del Benaco reaches the Verona shore in minutes.

highlights.title: Nature behind
highlights.body: The Valley of the Paper Mills and inland trails round off the stay.

gargnano.intro1: Gargnano is a fishing village on the Brescia shore, loved by sailors and anyone seeking quiet: a small harbour, historic villas and the Alto Garda park behind it attract guests from northern Europe.

highlights.title: Sailing and the lake
highlights.body: Regattas and steady winds draw sailors from all over Europe.

highlights.title: A quiet village
highlights.body: Away from traffic, it is the choice for silence and authenticity.

highlights.title: Nature and trails
highlights.body: The Alto Garda Bresciano park offers hikes a few steps from the lake.

tignale.intro1: Tignale is a panoramic plateau on the Brescia shore, with the Montecastello sanctuary perched above the lake: nature, trails and spectacular views attract hikers and anyone seeking peace.

highlights.title: Unique views
highlights.body: The views from the plateau are among the most spectacular on the lake.

highlights.title: Hiking and nature
highlights.body: Trails and cycling routes bring active guests from spring to autumn.

highlights.title: Peace and quiet
highlights.body: Ideal for guests who want to switch off, away from the crowds.

tremosine-sul-garda.intro1: Tremosine sul Garda, with the Strada della Forra and its viewing terrace over the lake, is for lovers of nature and sport: plateau villages, trails and scenic roads draw active guests.

highlights.title: Scenic roads
highlights.body: The Strada della Forra and the lake terraces are among the most photographed experiences on Lake Garda.

highlights.title: Outdoor sport
highlights.body: Hiking, cycling and climbing bring guests over a long season.

highlights.title: Plateau villages
highlights.body: Homes with views and quiet a few minutes from the lake.

limone-sul-garda.intro1: Limone sul Garda is one of the best-known places on the northern lake: the lemon houses, the harbour village and the cycle path suspended over the water draw guests from around the world over a long season.

highlights.title: International fame
highlights.body: A name known abroad: guests search for it before they even leave.

highlights.title: The cycle path over the lake
highlights.body: The cantilevered path over the water is an attraction that brings visitors all season.

highlights.title: High demand
highlights.body: Few homes are available compared with demand: prices and occupancy stay high.

calvagese-della-riviera.intro1: Calvagese della Riviera, inland between Lonato and Desenzano, combines hills, golf and spacious farmhouses: a choice for those who want quiet and greenery a short drive from the lake.

highlights.title: Golf and hills
highlights.body: The golf course nearby brings discerning guests outside summer too.

highlights.title: Spacious farmhouses
highlights.body: Country houses and villas with gardens suit families and groups.

highlights.title: Close to Desenzano
highlights.body: The lake, station and motorway are a few minutes' drive away.

castiglione-delle-stiviere.intro1: Castiglione delle Stiviere, on the morainic hills south of the lake, is the town where the idea of the Red Cross was born: minutes from Desenzano and Sirmione, with more accessible purchase prices and guests coming for tourism, work and events.

highlights.title: Close to the lake, accessible prices
highlights.body: Desenzano, Sirmione and the beaches are a quarter of an hour away: attractive returns on a smaller investment.

highlights.title: History and hills
highlights.body: The Red Cross museum, Solferino and the morainic hills bring visitors outside the season too.

highlights.title: Not just holidays
highlights.body: Local companies and services bring business stays all year.

carpenedolo.intro1: Carpenedolo, on the plain between Lonato, Montichiari and Castiglione, offers spacious, quiet homes a short drive from the lake and the airport: a convenient base for families, groups and business travellers.

highlights.title: Space and quiet
highlights.body: Detached houses and villas with gardens host families and groups who stay longer.

highlights.title: Strategic location
highlights.body: Lake Garda, Brescia and Montichiari airport are a few minutes' drive away.

highlights.title: Demand all year
highlights.body: Trade fairs, companies and local events fill the calendar outside the season too.

montichiari.intro1: Montichiari, with its airport, the Centro Fiera del Garda and Bonoris Castle, combines tourism and business: minutes from Desenzano and the lake, it draws holidaymakers, exhibitors and trade-fair visitors all year.

highlights.title: Trade fairs and events
highlights.body: The Centro Fiera del Garda brings exhibitors and visitors in many weeks of the year.

highlights.title: Airport and connections
highlights.body: The nearby airport and motorway make arrivals easy, even for a weekend.

highlights.title: The lake close by
highlights.body: Desenzano and the southern shore are about a quarter of an hour's drive away.
